title: Nuevo Laredo paid 22.3 million pesos to a company the U.S. Treasury links to the Northeast Cartel
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's city government awarded 22.3 million pesos in contracts to an asphalt company the U.S. Treasury lists as linked to the Northeast Cartel, according to records reviewed by LatinUS.
content:
The city government of Nuevo Laredo awarded 22.3 million pesos in public contracts to a company the United States Treasury Department links to the Northeast Cartel, according to municipal contracting records reviewed by the investigative outlet LatinUS.

The company, Concretos y Productos Asfálticos del Norte, received six contracts between 2024 and 2026 during the administration of Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, LatinUS reported after reviewing records on Mexico's National Transparency Platform.

Three of those contracts were awarded in 2026 alone, totaling 9.4 million pesos for asphalt resurfacing work on streets across Nuevo Laredo. Three more contracts in 2025, worth 4.3 million pesos each, added another 12.9 million pesos for asphalt work, according to the report.

The company was founded by Gamaliel Garza García, one of four people the U.S. Treasury included on a list released this month of individuals and companies it says are linked to the Northeast Cartel. According to the Treasury, both Concretos y Productos Asfálticos del Norte and a second Garza García company, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elías, were among the few construction companies authorized by the cartel to carry out construction work in Nuevo Laredo.

Webb Watch 956 reported earlier this month on the U.S. Treasury sanctions against the Northeast Cartel network. The new contracting records raise a separate question: how a company now flagged by Washington kept winning city asphalt work across the river, and whether Nuevo Laredo's contracting reviews check federal sanctions lists before awarding public money.

Being named on a U.S. sanctions list is not a criminal conviction, and the records reviewed by LatinUS do not by themselves prove wrongdoing in any individual contract. But the contracts are public money, and the pattern — six awards over three years to a company founded by a man Washington now identifies as part of a cartel-linked network — is exactly the kind of spending residents on both sides of the border deserve to see explained.

Webb Watch 956 has asked what review, if any, Nuevo Laredo applies to sanctions lists in its procurement process. As of publication, the city had not publicly addressed the LatinUS findings.

Sources:

  • Sonora Presente, "Nuevo Laredo government awarded 22.3 million pesos to company linked to the Northeast Cartel," Oct. 14, 2026 (reporting LatinUS records review)
